classification.difficultyReason: Plot seven explicitly supplied linear rules on common axes, then recognise their sharedpoint and verify it by directx=0 substitution. The relationship question is explicit and uses familiar taught substitution rather than a new general proof.

content.prompt: Draw and compare the following straight-line graphs.

children.prompt: Use the same set of axes to draw the graphs of:

spec.sourceRegion: Common response graph for the supplied rules
spec.description: One native blank square grid. No axes, scales or plotted answers are supplied.
spec.mathematics: Use one common coordinate plane for all supplied lines.

answer.short: $(-1,0),\ (0,2),\ (1,4)$. Solid line on the common graph.
answer.worked: Substitute $x=-1, 0, 1$ into $y=2x+2$ to obtain $y=0, 2, 4$. Plot $(-1,0),\ (0,2),\ (1,4)$ and draw the line on the same axes as the other parts.

answer.short: $(-1,3),\ (0,2),\ (1,1)$. Dashed line on the common graph.
answer.worked: Substitute $x=-1, 0, 1$ into $y=-x+2$ to obtain $y=3, 2, 1$. Plot $(-1,3),\ (0,2),\ (1,1)$ and draw the line on the same axes as the other parts.

answer.short: $(-2,1),\ (0,2),\ (2,3)$. Dotted line on the common graph.
answer.worked: Substitute $x=-2, 0, 2$ into $y=\frac12x+2$ to obtain $y=1, 2, 3$. Plot $(-2,1),\ (0,2),\ (2,3)$ and draw the line on the same axes as the other parts.

answer.short: $(-4,3),\ (0,2),\ (4,1)$. Dash-dot line on the common graph.
answer.worked: Substitute $x=-4, 0, 4$ into $y=-\frac14x+2$ to obtain $y=3, 2, 1$. Plot $(-4,3),\ (0,2),\ (4,1)$ and draw the line on the same axes as the other parts.

answer.short: $(-1,-1),\ (0,2),\ (1,5)$. Dash-dot-dot line on the common graph.
answer.worked: Substitute $x=-1, 0, 1$ into $y=3x+2$ to obtain $y=-1, 2, 5$. Plot $(-1,-1),\ (0,2),\ (1,5)$ and draw the line on the same axes as the other parts.

answer.short: $(-1,5),\ (0,2),\ (1,-1)$. Loosely dashed line on the common graph.
answer.worked: Substitute $x=-1, 0, 1$ into $y=2-3x$ to obtain $y=5, 2, -1$. Plot $(-1,5),\ (0,2),\ (1,-1)$ and draw the line on the same axes as the other parts.

answer.short: $(-3,3),\ (0,2),\ (3,1)$. Densely dotted line on the common graph.
answer.worked: Substitute $x=-3, 0, 3$ into $y=2-\frac13x$ to obtain $y=3, 2, 1$. Plot $(-3,3),\ (0,2),\ (3,1)$ and draw the line on the same axes as the other parts.

spec.description: All supplied lines use exactly one coordinate plane and unchanged scales. Their editable per-part answer names the corresponding line style, avoiding text on plotted ink.

children.label: h
children.prompt: What is the relationship between these straight-line graphs?

answer.short: They are all concurrent: they all pass through $(0,2)$.
answer.worked: Substituting $x=0$ into every supplied equation gives $y=2$. Hence every plotted line passes through $(0,2)$, so the lines are concurrent at that point.
